title: Collections: what we know so far
idea: Review-leaning finale for the MEET unit. Recap: when to use a list, how to write one, order, printing. Interleaves print and variables.

exercises.prompt: Recap: a list is best when a problem is about...
options: Many values of the same kind, together
exercises.explanation: Lists shine for groups: many scores, many prices, many names. One value still just uses a plain variable.

exercises.prompt: Recap: which is a correctly written list?
exercises.explanation: Square brackets and commas: [2, 4, 6]. That's the shape of every list.

exercises.prompt: Recap: a list keeps its items in the order you wrote them.
exercises.explanation: Order is dependable — the list never rearranges itself. That reliability sets up the next unit, indexing.
The list prints in its written order, with brackets: [8, 3, 5]. No sorting, no summing.

exercises.prompt: Recap: which problems want a list (pick all)?
exercises.explanation: 'All 20 students' and 'each hour' are groups — lists. The single lucky number and one winning ticket are single values.

exercises.prompt:
Review a variable from Lap 1. Predict:

level = 3
level = level + 1
print(level)
exercises.explanation: level starts at 3, then becomes 3 + 1 = 4. Reassignment still works just as before — lists didn't change that.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of code to what it makes.
exercises.explanation: No brackets means a single value; brackets mean a list, whether it holds one item or many.
First print shows the label, second shows the whole list. Two prints, two lines. Printing a list never sums it.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the thinking steps for a 'many values' problem, start to finish.
blocks: Notice the problem is about a group of values
Write the values into a list, in order
Store the list in a well-named variable
exercises.explanation: Recognize the group, write the list faithfully, give it a clear name. That's the whole MEET skill in three steps.

exercises.prompt: You can recognize, write, and print a list. What's the very next power you'll gain?
options: Grabbing one item by its position (first, third, last)
Storing a value with no name
exercises.explanation: Next up: indexing — reaching into the list to pull out a single item by its spot. You're ready for it!
